subject: ent
title: Sinonasal tumours and granulomatous conditions

steps.tx: Benign sinonasal tumours present with unilateral obstruction, discharge and epistaxis. **Inverted papilloma** arises from lateral nasal wall or maxillary sinus in middle aged men, locally destructive with about 5 to 10 percent synchronous or metachronous squamous carcinoma association, needing complete endoscopic excision including bony origin drilling and long surveillance for recurrence. Osteomas (frontal, incidental) and juvenile angiofibroma (adolescent males) complete classic benign patterns.
steps.say: One sided middle aged mass is inverted papilloma until proven otherwise: remove fully, watch for years, some turn malignant.

steps.tx: **Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma** grows from sphenopalatine foramen region in teenage boys (androgen sensitive, almost exclusively male), causing recurrent heavy epistaxis and obstruction with vascular blush on imaging (CT erosion, MRI flow voids, angiography feeding vessels from internal maxillary). Biopsy in clinic is forbidden for haemorrhage risk; preoperative embolisation precedes endoscopic resection in modern pathways.
steps.say: Teen boy, blocked nose, flooding bleeds: angiofibroma. Image and embolise, never biopsy in clinic.

steps.tx: Sinonasal **malignancies** (squamous carcinoma commonest, adenocarcinoma in hardwood workers ethmoid, olfactory neuroblastoma from olfactory cleft, mucosal melanoma, lymphoma) present late with unilateral epistaxis, obstruction, facial pain, orbital invasion (proptosis, diplopia), loose teeth or palatal mass and anosmia. Nickel and hardwood dust, leather work and HPV or EBV associations vary by type. MRI distinguishes tumour from trapped secretions; CT maps bone; biopsy via endoscopy after imaging vascular lesions excluded.
steps.say: Wood dust gives ethmoid adenocarcinoma. Late one sided bleeding with eye or tooth signs is cancer until scoped and biopsied safely.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Granulomatous and destructive midline disease includes granulomatosis with polyangiitis (septal perforation, saddle, crusting), cocaine induced midline lesions (history, ANCA artefacts), extranodal NK or T cell lymphoma nasal type (EBV linked, necrotic midline, formerly lethal midline granuloma) and sarcoid or tuberculosis mimics. Workup biopsies necrotic edges repeatedly (often non diagnostic), ANCA, cultures and EBV studies with rheumatology and haematology. Rhinoscleroma and rhinosporidiosis are regional infective masses in endemic patterns.
steps.say: Midline nose destruction: vasculitis, cocaine, lymphoma or infection. Biopsy edges, test ANCA and EBV.
